title: Whatever is newly introduced is rejected
cue: What becomes of something added to the religion that is not of it
arabic: عَنْ أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أُمِّ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا قَالَتْ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِي أَمْرِنَا هَذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ».
translation: It is narrated from the Mother of the Believers, Umm Abd Allah Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that is not of it, it is rejected.”

witnesses.name: ibn-daqiq-sharh
witnesses.ref: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in, Mu'assasat al-Rayyan 2003, hadith 5, p. 41: https://shamela.ws/book/11244/31

witnesses.name: haytami-fath-al-mubin
witnesses.ref: al-Haytami, al-Fath al-Mubin, Dar al-Minhaj 2008, hadith 5, p. 220: https://shamela.ws/book/8889/216

provenance.note: Hashes are of each witness's text of this narration, from al-Nawawi's opening words to the end before his attribution line, with honorific formulas written as we print them (ﷺ, رضي الله عنه): see data-sources/hadith-arabic/SOURCE.md. All three witnesses agree with ours. The variant is the wording al-Nawawi gives as "in a narration of Muslim".

notes.text: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id calls this [[hadith]] a great rule of the religion and one of the Prophet's ﷺ concise, comprehensive sayings: it plainly rejects every innovation and invented practice.

source.work: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyya

variants.label: In a narration of Muslim: “Whoever does a deed that is not in keeping with our matter, it is rejected.”
variants.arabic: مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ
